title: Date parser: slash dates, partial dates, age-at-date
body:
## Context
SOP P5, P6, P7 compare dates part by part: unknown parts never contradict. `normalize/dates.py` parses ISO, year, `Month D, YYYY`, `D Month YYYY` but not slash dates or ages. Every DOB, temporal and deceased rule depends on this being right (risks R1-R3 in the plan).

## Files to touch
- `system/screening/normalize/dates.py` (primary)
- `tests/test_dates.py` (new)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `DD/MM/YYYY` parsed day-first (also `D/M/YYYY`, `DD-MM-YYYY`, `DD.MM.YYYY`)
- [ ] `YYYY-MM`, `Month YYYY`, `Mon. D YYYY`, ordinal days (`3rd March 1980`) parsed as partial dates
- [ ] `birth_years_from_age(age, PartialDate) -> tuple[int, int]` returns (y-age-1, y-age): aged 45 in March 2019 gives 1973 or 1974
- [ ] `dates_agree(customer, hit)` and `dates_contradict(customer, hit)` helpers implementing P6/P7 (year +-1 rule; month/day only compared in the same year)
- [ ] unparseable input returns None, never raises
- [ ] unit tests in `tests/test_dates.py`
- [ ] `python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev` shows 0 unsafe clearances
- [ ] `python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev` byte-identical
- [ ] stdlib only, no new dependencies under system/

## How to verify
```bash
# data/dev is your local (gitignored) copy of the dev data folder
python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'system');from screening.normalize.dates import parse_date as p;print(p('07/02/1989'),p('1968-02'),p('March 2019'))"
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev -v
python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev
```

## Hints
- Slash dates in customers/KYC/notes: second number is NEVER >12, first is >12 in ~6.3k customer values, so the format is DD/MM. 4.7k customer values are ambiguous (both <=12): still DD/MM
- customers.dob mix: ISO 55%, slash 15%, `D Month YYYY` 15%, `Month D, YYYY` 15%, year-only 28, null 30. kyc.verified_dob is null on 1,850 checks
- hits.dobs is a `;` list already split by `contracts.as_list`: mostly year-only (240) or ISO (50) or `YYYY-MM` (3)
- deceased_date can be `YYYY-MM`
- Keep `PartialDate` frozen and ordered; don't change its public fields (contract change)

Plan and counts: `docs/specs/2026-11-21-engine-plan.md`.

title: Country normaliser: codes, demonyms, long tail
body:
## Context
SOP P6 location: codes and nationalities are countries; territories count as their own country; "International"/"Europe" are not countries. Location is the biggest clearing reason in the practice labels (18 of 28 DIFFERENT). An unknown value collapsing to None or to a different spelling is the main unsafe-clearance risk (R5, R7).

## Files to touch
- `system/screening/normalize/countries.py` (primary)
- `tests/test_countries.py` (new)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ISO-2 and ISO-3 codes, English names, common alternates (`Cote D'Ivoire`/`Ivory Coast`, `Russia`/`Russian Federation`, `UAE`, `Viet Nam`) and demonyms (`Nigerian`, `British`, `Bangladeshi`, `Irish`, `Polish`, `Brazilian`...) map to one canonical name for all ~200 countries and main territories
- [ ] `[Associated]`-style bracket tags and surrounding punctuation are stripped
- [ ] unknown values return a stable canonical string (casefolded, accents stripped), never None
- [ ] `find_countries(text) -> list[str]` scans free text for country names AND demonyms (used by search-result and notes extraction)
- [ ] territories (Hong Kong, Puerto Rico, Gibraltar, Jersey, ...) stay separate countries
- [ ] unit tests in `tests/test_countries.py`
- [ ] `python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev` shows 0 unsafe clearances
- [ ] `python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev` byte-identical
- [ ] stdlib only, no new dependencies under system/

## How to verify
```bash
# data/dev is your local (gitignored) copy of the dev data folder
python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'system');from screening.normalize.countries import normalize_country as n;print(n('NG'),n('Nigerian'),n('United States [Associated]'),n('Europe'))"
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev -v
python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev
```

## Hints
- customers.nationality: 81 values, names and demonyms mixed (Nigerian 3,023, British 2,307, Bangladeshi 2,265)
- customers.residence_country: 90 values, names and ISO-2 mixed (US 2,797, NG 2,778, GB 2,696, ES, DE, FR, BD, IT, IE, CA, AU)
- kyc.document_country is always a full name; KYC notes use demonyms (`using a Nigerian national ID`)
- Search snippets phrase countries many ways: `in Pakistan`, `within Cote D'Ivoire`, `a Netherlands resident`, `Brazilian authorities`
- Keep the table as data (dict literal) so it is easy to review; no external files needed

Plan and counts: `docs/specs/2026-11-21-engine-plan.md`.

title: Name matcher (SOP P8): parts_match and names_agree
body:
## Context
SOP P8 defines name agreement exactly: parts ignoring case/accents/punctuation/brackets; initials are not parts; variants from name_variants.json; joined/split parts (Abdulsalam = Abdul Salam, one part covering both); edit distance 1 for 4-6 letters, 2 for 7+, exact below 4 (shorter part decides; transposition = 2 edits); agree when >=2 parts match or every part of the shorter name matches; placeholders are not parts; company legal forms are not parts. Both rule-name and P7 confirmation depend on this; no SAME_ENTITY is possible without it.

## Files to touch
- `system/screening/normalize/names.py` (primary)
- `tests/test_names.py` (new)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `parts_match` and `names_agree` implemented, returning `NameMatch` (with `fuzzy=True` when any pair matched only by edit distance)
- [ ] variant groups and legal forms loaded once from `name_variants.json` (path from the Dataset / data dir, cached, deterministic)
- [ ] plain Levenshtein (no Damerau): `ahmde` vs `ahmed` is 2 edits
- [ ] joined/split handled both ways (customer `Abdul Salam` vs hit `Abdulsalam` and vice versa), counting as one matched part
- [ ] each distinct part matched at most once (one-to-one assignment, deterministic tie-break)
- [ ] `real_part_count(name)` helper so rules can apply the fewer-than-two-real-parts guard
- [ ] tests cover: `CHINEDU AZEEZ` vs `Ridwan, Azeez` -> NOT agree (only 1 of 2 matched); `Mohammad Nadeem` vs `Muhammad Nadeem` -> agree; `XXX MARTON XXX` has 1 real part
- [ ] unit tests in `tests/test_names.py`
- [ ] `python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev` shows 0 unsafe clearances
- [ ] `python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev` byte-identical
- [ ] stdlib only, no new dependencies under system/

## How to verify
```bash
# data/dev is your local (gitignored) copy of the dev data folder
python -m unittest tests.test_names -v
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev -v
python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev
```

## Hints
- Hit names are often `Surname, Given` (`Costa, Marcos Roberto`); the comma is just punctuation
- Screened names contain placeholders: `UNKNOWN NADEEM`, `BROOKS N/A`, `AZAM NA NA`, `RAHMAN TEST TEST`, `BUSTAMANTE 0000`
- 297 of 819 hits have aliases; aliases (incl. single-part nicknames) count as names
- KYC/notes names are UPPER CASE; profile text has accents (`Paweł`, `Thuận Thị Lê`)
- name_variants.json has `given_names` groups and a legal-forms list; read its keys rather than hard-coding

Plan and counts: `docs/specs/2026-11-21-engine-plan.md`.

title: Customer resolution: unlinked alerts + joint-account candidate filtering
body:
## Context
SOP P2: follow the alert's link; a link can lead to several people and the screened details pick between them; with no link, find records whose full/preferred/login name agrees (P8), DOB equal in every shared part, screened country as residence or nationality, screened city in city/address. Never use another customer's records. Today 146 unlinked alerts resolve to nobody and 58 joint-account alerts keep both holders.

## Files to touch
- `system/screening/resolve.py` (primary)
- `system/screening/loaders.py` (only to add a name-part index)
- `tests/test_resolve.py` (new)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] unlinked alerts: candidate search via an index on name parts (built once in `Dataset.build_indexes`), filtered by every screened detail that is present (name P8, DOB parts, country, city)
- [ ] linked alerts with >1 customer: keep only those the screened name and DOB fit; if none fit, keep all (P3 then yields AMBIGUOUS)
- [ ] `Resolution.path` records each step in the wording of the practice-label `path` (for the dashboard)
- [ ] falls back to exact-token name matching until `names_agree` lands (guarded try/except NotImplementedError)
- [ ] alerts with no screened DOB (188) still resolve on name + country/city
- [ ] dev: the 12 practice labels with path `name, date of birth, country and city` and the 8 joint-account labels resolve to the labelled record (or AMBIGUOUS for the 2 `different people fit` cases)
- [ ] unit tests in `tests/test_resolve.py`
- [ ] `python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev` shows 0 unsafe clearances
- [ ] `python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev` byte-identical
- [ ] stdlib only, no new dependencies under system/

## How to verify
```bash
# data/dev is your local (gitignored) copy of the dev data folder
python system/screen.py explain H-582410 --data data/dev
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev -v
python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev
```

## Hints
- Link types are exclusive: account_ref 170, login_handle 70, email 54, none 146
- Only 52 accounts in the bank are joint but 58 alerts point at one: these are planted
- customers.login_name is never filled; preferred_name is filled on 16k records
- Screened DOB may be year-only (34) or `D Month YYYY`; compare only shared parts
- 72k customers: build indexes once; avoid O(alerts x customers) scans

Plan and counts: `docs/specs/2026-11-21-engine-plan.md`.

title: Identity graph (SOP P3): merge records by phone+DOB or approved document number
body:
## Context
SOP P3: records sharing a phone AND the same full DOB are one person; so are records whose approved identity checks carry the same document number; transitively. Shared phone or address alone does not link (family). All facts of the merged person count. 13 of 50 practice-label paths merge two records; missing a merge drops countries and verified names, which leads to false LOCATION clears (R5).

## Files to touch
- `system/screening/identity.py` (new, primary)
- `system/screening/resolve.py` (one call site in build_person/resolve_customer)
- `tests/test_identity.py` (new)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] union-find over all customers, built once per Dataset, deterministic (sorted ids)
- [ ] edges: (normalised phone, full parsed DOB) and (document_number on approved KYC reached via onboarding -> applicant)
- [ ] no edge on phone alone, address alone, or partial DOB
- [ ] `resolve_customer` expands each candidate to its full group before deciding; `Person.record_ids` lists all
- [ ] dev: the 13 `one person:` practice-label paths produce exactly those record groups
- [ ] unit tests in `tests/test_identity.py`
- [ ] `python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev` shows 0 unsafe clearances
- [ ] `python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev` byte-identical
- [ ] stdlib only, no new dependencies under system/

## How to verify
```bash
# data/dev is your local (gitignored) copy of the dev data folder
python system/screen.py explain H-0181BD --data data/dev
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev -v
python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev
```

## Hints
- 164 phone numbers are shared across customer records; most are family, not the same person
- DOBs are in four formats on different records of the same person: compare parsed dates, not strings (use parse_date; until date-parser lands ISO-only is fine)
- Phone formats look like `+34 681419534`; normalise to digits
- KYC links via onboarding: customer -> accounts -> onboarding.kyc_applicant_id -> kyc_checks.applicant_id

Plan and counts: `docs/specs/2026-11-21-engine-plan.md`.

title: Verified identity from KYC checks and onboarding notes (SOP P4) + notes residence
body:
## Context
SOP P4: the most recent APPROVED identity check gives legal name, DOB and document country, whether it is in kyc_checks or only in a note by the onboarding team; rejected/expired are not evidence; verified name outranks record and screened name. SOP P6 location also counts "places the notes say they lived". 21 of 50 practice labels cite a NOTE as the deciding source.

## Files to touch
- `system/screening/normalize/notes.py` (new, primary)
- `system/screening/resolve.py` (add `Person.verified` and `Person.note_countries` properties only)
- `tests/test_notes.py` (new)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `parse_kyc_note(text, created_at) -> VerifiedIdentity | None` extracts name, DOB (raw + parsed), document country, check date, provider
- [ ] anchor-based extraction (DOB/born + date, UPPER-CASE name run, country lexicon/demonym), not a fixed template list; >= 98% of `channel: kyc` notes in dev parse
- [ ] notes that say rejected / failed / expired / could not verify are skipped
- [ ] `Person.verified` = newest of approved kyc_checks and parsed KYC notes (by check date, then id); carries the source id (KYC-... or NOTE-...) for evidence
- [ ] `extract_residence_countries(text)` returns countries from residence/employment statements (`lived and worked in X`, `resident and employee in X`, `job and home in X`)
- [ ] tests include at least 10 differently-worded KYC notes and 5 residence notes (paraphrased, not copied)
- [ ] unit tests in `tests/test_notes.py`
- [ ] `python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev` shows 0 unsafe clearances
- [ ] `python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev` byte-identical
- [ ] stdlib only, no new dependencies under system/

## How to verify
```bash
# data/dev is your local (gitignored) copy of the dev data folder
python system/screen.py explain H-582410 --data data/dev   # should cite NOTE-14E25A as DOB source
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev -v
python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev
```

## Hints
- 22.6k of 31.9k notes are channel kyc and ALL are successes in dev; rejected/expired exist only in kyc_checks (2,481 + 2,433). The unseen set may differ: guard anyway
- Shapes: `ID check complete: <Provider> processed <doc> (<Country>) for <NAME>, DOB <date>, on <iso>.` / `<doc> from <Country> verified by <Provider> on <iso> for <NAME>, DOB <date>.` / `<NAME>'s identity was confirmed via <Provider> on <iso> using a <Demonym> <doc>. DOB recorded as <date>.` / `<iso>: <Provider> confirmed <doc> for <NAME>, DOB <date>, ctry <Country>.`
- Providers: Persona, Onfido, Veriff, Sumsub. Documents: passport, national ID, driving licence
- Notes link to customers ONLY by requester_email = customers.email
- ~2.3k non-kyc notes are residence statements in many wordings; the rest are support chatter (`card payment was declined` - not a KYC result!)

Plan and counts: `docs/specs/2026-11-21-engine-plan.md`.

title: Hit facts: profile-note DOBs/ages, dated reports, search-result filtering (SOP P5)
body:
## Context
SOP P5: a hit's DOB is its `dobs`, else a sentence in the FIRST paragraph of profile_notes (age at a date gives two years), else web search results that describe the same kind of listing (phrase from primary category, else first category) in a country tied to the hit. Dated reports are exactly English lines `According to ...; September 10, 2025: ...`; other wordings do not count. Search-result phrases and the dated-report form are worded the same in the unseen set; everything else may be reworded.

## Files to touch
- `system/screening/facts.py` (primary)
- `tests/test_facts.py` (new)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `HitFacts` gains `dob_candidates` (parsed, each with source `dobs` | `profile_notes` | `SR-...`), `dated_reports` (earliest first, with date), `relevant_search_results`
- [ ] first paragraph = text before the first blank line; `born in YYYY`, `born on <date>` and any sentence with an age number plus a `Month YYYY` give candidates
- [ ] dated-report regex matches only `^According to <src>; <Month> <D>, <YYYY>:` per line
- [ ] search result kept only if its snippet contains the hit's listing phrase AND a country tied to the hit (via `find_countries`), and it is only used when no dobs / notes DOB exist; marked weak
- [ ] `dob_sources` stays parallel and evidence ids (SR-...) are carried
- [ ] dev: H-D861DA and H-4AA437 (labels citing profile-note birth years) and the 5 SR-cited labels produce the labelled years
- [ ] unit tests in `tests/test_facts.py`
- [ ] `python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev` shows 0 unsafe clearances
- [ ] `python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev` byte-identical
- [ ] stdlib only, no new dependencies under system/

## How to verify
```bash
# data/dev is your local (gitignored) copy of the dev data folder
python system/screen.py explain H-0181BD --data data/dev   # SR-590704 should be the only relevant result
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev -v
python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev
```

## Hints
- 431/819 hits have profile_notes, 214 have `According to` lines: 639 full-date lines, 23 `; Month YYYY:` and 143 other shapes - only the 639 count
- Ignore career ranges `(December 10, 2011 - May 02, 2018)`, `as of 2022/03/31` lines and Spanish/French duplicate sections (`Trayectoria:`)
- Age wordings vary: `aged 30, in November 1998`, `reached the age of N`, `was N years old`, `at age N`, `The age of X was N when ... in Month YYYY`
- Search snippets: `X, 27, ... in a September 2014 report`, `27-year-old X`, `Published in December 2007 ... X, 51`; each of the 6 listing phrases appears in ~1.1k snippets, mostly namesakes
- primary_category is null on 345 hits; `Registration` / `Other Segment` -> `named on a watchlist`
- Search results are keyed by the hit name's sorted lowercase parts (`search_query_key`)

Plan and counts: `docs/specs/2026-11-21-engine-plan.md`.

title: DOB rule (SOP P6/P7): DOB_MISMATCH and DOB agreement
body:
## Context
SOP P6: clear on DOB only if EVERY hit birth date is contradicted (customer year more than 1 outside, or same year with different month/day); one agreeing date prevents it. P7: agree when the customer year is one of the hit's possible years and every shared part is equal. Customer DOB = latest approved verified DOB (P4), else record DOB. Company: dobs is an incorporation date only.

## Files to touch
- `system/screening/rules/dob.py` (primary)
- `tests/test_rule_dob.py` (new)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CONTRADICTION (`DOB_MISMATCH`) / AGREEMENT / abstain per the SOP, over all hit DOB candidates (dobs, notes ages as 2-year sets, search results)
- [ ] uses the verified DOB when present and cites its id (KYC-/NOTE-), else the customer record
- [ ] abstains when either side has no parseable DOB
- [ ] `weak=True, weak_why="DOB_FROM_SEARCH_RESULT"` when the deciding hit DOB came from a search result
- [ ] summary sentence in the style `The customer's date of birth is 1979-11-08 (NOTE-...) but the hit's profile notes put its birth year at 1976 or 1977.`
- [ ] tests built from hand-made `Context`s (no dataset needed): year-only vs full, +-1 boundary, same-year month mismatch, mixed agree+contradict -> no clear
- [ ] unit tests in `tests/test_rule_dob.py`
- [ ] `python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev` shows 0 unsafe clearances
- [ ] `python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev` byte-identical
- [ ] stdlib only, no new dependencies under system/

## How to verify
```bash
# data/dev is your local (gitignored) copy of the dev data folder
python -m unittest tests.test_rule_dob -v
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev -v
python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev
```

## Hints
- Write against `parse_date` / `PartialDate` and `HitFacts.dobs_raw`; once hit-facts lands switch to `dob_candidates`
- Hit dob pairs like `1996; 1997` are common: the customer year must be outside BOTH by >1
- 7 dev labels are DOB_MISMATCH (3 from listed dob, 2 from profile notes, 2 from search results)
- Never use alerts.dob when a verified DOB exists

Plan and counts: `docs/specs/2026-11-21-engine-plan.md`.

title: Name rule (SOP P6/P8): NAME_MISMATCH_VERIFIED and name agreement
body:
## Context
SOP P6 name: different entity when the customer's VERIFIED legal name agrees with none of the hit's names or aliases (P8), even if the record name does. P7 needs name agreement to confirm: agreement may come from the verified name, record full/preferred names or the screened name. Placeholder-only names (<2 real parts) can be neither confirmed nor cleared.

## Files to touch
- `system/screening/rules/name.py` (primary)
- `tests/test_rule_name.py` (new)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CONTRADICTION only from the latest approved verified name (KYC or note) vs every hit name and alias; abstain without a verified name
- [ ] AGREEMENT when any customer name (verified first) agrees with any hit name/alias; `weak=True` if the match is fuzzy
- [ ] <2 real parts on the individual customer side -> abstain (but a hit's single-part alias can still agree)
- [ ] company names: legal forms ignored
- [ ] summary in the style `The customer's verified name is X (KYC-...), which does not match the hit's name Y.` / `The customer's name agrees with the hit's name Y.`
- [ ] until `names_agree` is implemented the rule abstains (catch NotImplementedError)
- [ ] unit tests in `tests/test_rule_name.py`
- [ ] `python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev` shows 0 unsafe clearances
- [ ] `python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev` byte-identical
- [ ] stdlib only, no new dependencies under system/

## How to verify
```bash
# data/dev is your local (gitignored) copy of the dev data folder
python -m unittest tests.test_rule_name -v
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev -v
python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev
```

## Hints
- 7 dev labels clear on verified name, e.g. verified `SARAH JOHNSON` vs hit `Johnson, James Jacob` (1 part) and `Jonathan Reyes Whitfield` vs `John Whitfield` (John/Jonathan are not variants or within 1 edit)
- All 10 dev REVIEW labels have name + country agreement but no comparable DOB: name agreement alone must never confirm a person
- Screened name examples with placeholders: `UNKNOWN NADEEM`, `XXX MARTON XXX`

Plan and counts: `docs/specs/2026-11-21-engine-plan.md`.

title: Location rule (SOP P6/P7): LOCATION_MISMATCH and country agreement
body:
## Context
SOP P6 location: different entity when EVERY country tied to the customer (residence and nationality on all records of the person, approved identity document country, places notes say they lived) differs from EVERY country tied to the hit (countries, nationality, citizenship, last part of addresses, place_of_birth). A country difference does not clear a hit whose name and DOB agree (compiler already enforces). Company confirmation needs name + country (P7).

## Files to touch
- `system/screening/rules/location.py` (primary)
- `tests/test_rule_location.py` (new)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] builds the customer set from all `Person.records`, `Person.verified` doc country and notes residence countries (when those land; use what exists, never fewer than the records)
- [ ] both sets normalised via `normalize_country`; NOT_COUNTRIES dropped; abstain if either set is empty
- [ ] CONTRADICTION `LOCATION_MISMATCH` when disjoint; AGREEMENT when they intersect (cite the shared country)
- [ ] evidence cites the customer record(s)/KYC/NOTE that contributed a country and the hit
- [ ] summary in the style `The customer is linked only to Netherlands but the hit is linked only to United States.`
- [ ] test: name+DOB agree and countries differ -> compiler gives REVIEW
- [ ] unit tests in `tests/test_rule_location.py`
- [ ] `python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev` shows 0 unsafe clearances
- [ ] `python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev` byte-identical
- [ ] stdlib only, no new dependencies under system/

## How to verify
```bash
# data/dev is your local (gitignored) copy of the dev data folder
python -m unittest tests.test_rule_location -v
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev -v
python system/screen.py repro --runs 5 --data data/dev
```

## Hints
- Largest dev bucket: 18 of 28 DIFFERENT labels accept LOCATION_MISMATCH
- Customer sets in labels often have 2 countries (`Bangladesh, United Kingdom`; `Ghana, Netherlands`) because of merged records or notes residence; miss one and you clear wrongly
- Hit addresses carry role tags `United States [Associated]` - facts.py strips them; keep it that way
- Long-tail hit countries (Moldova, Slovenia, Panama, Syria, UAE) appear in REVIEW labels: they must AGREE with the customer, not be dropped

Plan and counts: `docs/specs/2026-11-21-engine-plan.md`.

title: Deceased and temporal-impossibility rules (SOP P6 time)
body:
## Context
SOP P6 time: different entity when the customer was younger than 16 at the earliest dated report, or a company was incorporated after it; or the profile gives a date of death before the customer was screened. Dated reports are only the exact `According to ...; <Month D, YYYY>:` lines (P5).

## Files to touch
- `system/screening/rules/temporal.py` (primary)
- `system/screening/rules/deceased.py`
- `tests/test_rule_time.py` (new)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] TEMPORAL: earliest dated report vs customer's latest possible birth date (verified DOB first); clear only if the customer is under 16 even in the most favourable reading; company: incorporation (`dobs`) after the report
- [ ] DECEASED: parsed `deceased_date` strictly before `alerts.screened_at` comparing only shared parts; `life_status: Deceased` without a date -> abstain
- [ ] both abstain on any missing or unparseable input
- [ ] summary in the style `The customer was born in 2007 (KYC-...), so they were at most 13 when the hit's profile reports activity on 2020-01-08.`
- [ ] unit tests in `tests/test_rule_time.py`
- [ ] `python system/screen.py eval --data data/dev` shows 0 unsafe clearances
